chapter: Building the band in New York
title: Learning ensemble technique and recording; early records all heads
summary: Buck Clayton's quote that the band was not always in tune on arrival in New York; Basie says the first successful recordings were all heads.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I think we're going to what he said, which I'm sure you'll corroborate, which is that "some of us had come in with patched up horns, instruments tied together and such things." Oh, he says here. "When the Basie band first came to New York, we didn't even sound in tune all the time." Is that true?
"We had to learn how to choose

good instruments and we had to learn how to record properly."
Well, that makes sense, doesn't it? I mean, you were a new band.

Joe talking now. "Basie band had the feel of a small band. The arrangements were almost all heads." See, I guess this was until what? You got to New York? When you got to New York, you started getting arrangements, is that it?
Started doing -- the most successful things -- the first of our recordings were all heads.
